frames.narration: Short polling: the client asks every 2 seconds whether anything is new. Most of the time the server answers 'nothing'.
An update happens right after a poll. The client will not hear about it until the next poll, so it is up to 2 seconds late, and thousands of empty requests were spent to get there.

states.server: update waits for the next poll

frames.narration: Long polling: the client asks and the server holds the request open. Nothing is sent back until there is something to say.
The update happens. The server answers at once, and the client immediately sends a new request to wait again. Delivery is fast, at the price of a request cycle per update.
Server-sent events: one request stays open and the server streams events down it whenever it likes. The client reconnects by itself and resumes from the last event id.
WebSocket: an HTTP request is upgraded to a persistent two-way connection. Either side can send a small message at any time.
If the connection drops, a good client reconnects with backoff and jitter and asks for everything after the last id it received, so nothing is lost.
